minutes.headline: ZBA continued the Flat Hill shed appeal to Oct 23 and let Webb Motors withdraw its 36 Summer St permit request.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals continued an appeal by the Village at Flat Hill trustees over a shed on common land, after a resident objected to notification. It then heard Webb Motors' special permit request for auto repair and sales at 36 Summer Street. Members called it premature and the lot too congested, and the applicant withdrew without prejudice. The applicants were told they must return to the board to transfer the 40 Summer Street permit to the new owner's company.

public_comment.topic: Objected that the trustees put a shed on common land, said deeded-access owners were not notified, and asked that his email be read.
Said her nephew was a victim of the previous business and that promised fixes did not happen.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals let the Webb Motors applicant withdraw its 36 Summer Street special permit petition without prejudice, so it may return later.
Members had called the auto repair and sales request premature and the lot too congested before the withdrawal was granted.
The board voted to continue the Village at Flat Hill trustees' appeal over a shed on common land to October 23.
The applicants were told the existing 40 Summer Street permit can pass to the new owner's company only after they return to the board to document the change.
A resident objected that deeded-access owners were not notified of the shed, and another said promised fixes from the previous business did not happen.

why_it_matters: The Webb Motors request for auto repair and sales at 36 Summer Street is not decided, and because it was withdrawn without prejudice it can come back to the board as a new request.
The Flat Hill shed appeal, which turns on whether owners with deeded access to the common land were properly notified, stays open until the board's next hearing.
